item.title: Company expands recall of cat food that could cause serious illness
item.description: A recall of potentially harmful cat food has been expanded to include two additional lots of products, affecting 20 states, according to a Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announcement Friday.

item.title: Living Black History: WGN-TV honors centennial of Black History Month
item.description: It's been 100 years since historian and educator Carter G. Woodson started what would eventually be known as Black History Month. This month, WGN-TV has heard from a lot of authors and experts. This time, however, we wanted to hear from the people who have been witness to those 100 years of history.

item.description: NEW YORK (AP) — Neil Sedaka, the hit-making singer-songwriter whose boyish soprano and bright melodies made him a top act in the early years of rock ‘n' roll and led to a second run of success in the 1970s, has died. item.title: No longer free: Parking fees at Fashion Outlets of Chicago spark mixed reactions
item.description: You may want to plan ahead if you’re heading to the Fashion Outlets of Chicago in Rosemont. Parking is no longer free unless you’re staying for a short visit or spending a certain amount inside.

item.title: Suspect in murder of father, son outside Little Village jewelry store captured in St. Louis
item.description: A Chicago man wanted for the November 2025 murder of a father and son in Little Village is now in custody.

item.title: FAA considers capping summer flights at O’Hare ahead of busy schedule
item.description: The FAA is considering limiting flights at O'Hare International Airport this summer due to increased travel demand, which could lead to delays for travelers.

item.title: 20 injured in crash involving CTA bus on Chicago's South Side
item.description: Twenty people were injured in a crash Friday afternoon involving a CTA bus on the city's South Side.

item.title: Memorial services for Rev. Jesse Jackson continue Friday in Chicago
item.description: Mourners gathered in Chicago to pay their respects to the late civil rights leader Rev. Jesse Jackson Sr. as memorial services began in the city he called home.
